descriptionChirho: Basic Qal sense of visual perception, observation, looking, gazing, experiencing — Arabic ra'a / yara / nazara, Korean boda, Swahili kuona — covering all Qal finite forms, infinitives, imperatives, and active participles used predicatively.
Substantival use of the Qal active participle as a title meaning seer or prophet (roeh) — Arabic ra'iy, Korean boneun ja, Swahili mwonaji — a recognized prophetic office in ancient Israel.
Qal sense of seeing to a matter or providing, as in God will see to it / provide — Spanish proveerá, Swahili atajipatia, Arabic yara in providential context.
Nifal (passive/reflexive) stem meaning to appear, become visible, be seen, present oneself — Arabic zahara / yura, Korean boida / natanada, Swahili kuonekana.

labelChirho: Hifil: to show, cause to see
descriptionChirho: Hifil (causative) stem meaning to show, display, cause someone to see — Arabic ara (Form IV causative), Korean boyeojuda, Swahili kuonyesha.
Hofal (passive causative) stem meaning to be shown or made to see — Arabic urita (passive of Form IV), Korean boyeojin, Swahili kuonyeshwa.
